exposure: Pre-pregnancy left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF ≥55% vs LVEF <55%)
cohort: 146 women with peripartum cardiomyopathy, of which 50 had 75 subsequent pregnancies
finding: Subsequent pregnancies in women with a history of peripartum cardiomyopathy and recovered left ventricular systolic function are associated with a favorable outcome and low likelihood of maternal mortality, although a slight reduction in LVEF, mostly during the third trimester and persisting up to 6 months postpartum, was observed.
